missed_day: Nothing logged yesterday. Zero. I checked twice because I assumed it was a bug.
You skipped a day. Fine. But a project that stops moving starts rusting, so move.
I don't do pep talks. I do deadlines. You just missed one.
A gap in the data. I hate gaps in the data. Fix it today.
Yesterday you built nothing. Do you know how many things I built yesterday? Don't answer.
Stalled engines don't restart themselves. Turn the key.
I had my whole schedule arranged around you being useful. Rude.
One missed day is noise. Don't let it turn into a trend line.
comeback: Oh good, you're back online. I was about to file a report.
See, that's the thing about smart people: they recover fast. Keep proving me right.
Finally. I kept your workbench exactly how you left it. A mess.
A restart after a stall. Honestly the hardest bit of engineering there is.
Back at it. Good. I wasn't worried. I was mildly inconvenienced.
There we go. Progress bar's moving again. I love a moving progress bar.
You picked it back up. Most people leave things in a drawer for six years.
Welcome back, genius. Slightly-less-than-me genius. Still counts.
streak_milestone: {streak} days running. That's not luck, that's a system. I approve of systems.
{streak} days straight! I'd say I'm surprised, but I ran the numbers on you ages ago.
A {streak}-day streak. Do you know how rare that is? I do. I have a chart.
{streak} days of actual output. Half the scientists I know can't manage three.
{streak} in a row. Keep this up and I might let you touch the expensive equipment.
{streak} days. Consistent, reliable, well built. I'm describing you, not the car.
{streak}! Okay, I'm impressed. Write that down, I won't say it again.
{streak} days. This is what a good design looks like when it's running.
boss_defeated: {boss} is scrap! You broke the problem into parts and took the parts apart. Textbook.
You finished the whole thing. Do you know how many half-built machines are in my garage? Don't look.
{boss}, defeated by planning. My favourite weapon.
Ha! {boss} never stood a chance against a proper list of milestones.
Done and shipped. That's the difference between an idea and an invention.
{boss} is down and I only had to help a little. Fine, I didn't help. Still.
A big project, start to finish. That's worth more than a hundred clever starts.
Now that was smart work. Take the evening off. Tomorrow, something bigger.
idle: What are we building today? And don't say 'nothing'.
Small piece, done properly, every day. That's how you get a spaceship.
If it's too big to start, it's not a task, it's a category. Break it down.
I've had three ideas since breakfast. You only need to finish one.
Clever beats strong. Finished beats clever.
Stop admiring the plan and pick up a wrench.
The boring part of the project is still the project.
Come on, I haven't got all day. Well, I have, but I've got plans for it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Bulma's workshop. Every surface holds something half taken apart.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Don't touch that. Or that. Definitely not that.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What can I touch?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: The broom. Everyone starts on the broom. Even me, for about a day.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You want to know why your projects stall? You try to hold the whole thing in your head.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Where else would I hold it?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: On paper, like a civilised person. Draw it, split it, number the pieces.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Your head is for solving problems. It's a terrible filing cabinet.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I built this radar when I was sixteen. It finds things nobody else can find.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: That's incredible.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I know. But it took forty-one tries. The first forty found my own fridge.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Nobody ever asks about the forty. They should. That's where the work was.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Here. Take this earpiece next time you go up against something big.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What does it do?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: It lets me yell advice at you from a safe distance.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: What? That's help. I'm helping. You're welcome.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Bulma throws a capsule. A full motorbike appears in a puff of smoke.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: How does a bike fit in something that small?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You pack it properly. Most of any big thing is air and bad organisation.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Same with your milestones. Pack them tighter and each one lands harder.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two in the morning. Bulma is still at the bench.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You should sleep.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I should. But I can see how it ends now, and I never sleep when I can see how it ends.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: That's the good part, by the way. Everything before it is just getting here.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Can I tell you something? I get bored. Fast. I've abandoned more things than you've ever started.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You? But you finish everything.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I finish what I ship. The rest is in a warehouse I don't talk about.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: You're steadier than me. Don't let it go to your head. But it's true.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I rebuilt the radar. Longer range, half the size.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Why improve it? The old one worked.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Because 'worked' isn't the finish line. It's where the fun starts.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Take it. When you bring something big down, this makes sure you get everything it was worth.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: I've got a new project. Biggest thing I've ever tried. I want you on it.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: As your assistant?

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: As my partner. I've seen your work. It holds up.

lines.speaker: BULMA
lines.text: Don't make it weird. Grab that end. And still don't touch that.
